learnerFacingLabels.note: Localized learner-facing competency labels are not authored in v1. Competency IDs are never shown as interface copy. Learner-facing text in v1 is limited to objective titles and completion/mastery state copy.

families.name: Comprehension
families.scope: What the learner understood from what the other party said.

families.name: Interaction management
families.scope: How the learner runs the exchange itself.

families.name: Functional outcomes
families.scope: The real-world result the learner is trying to reach.

families.name: Language control
families.scope: Vocabulary, form, and coherence in service of meaning.

families.name: Learning strategy
families.scope: How the learner copes, repairs, and retrieves language.

competencies.observableCapability: Identifies an essential fact, question, offer, or requested detail and responds consistently with it.
Understands a limitation, condition, refusal, alternative, date, amount, or other constraint.
Follows connected information or more than one required action without losing the task.
Opens and closes an exchange appropriately for channel and register.
Makes the reason for the interaction understandable.
Supplies relevant personal, temporal, quantitative, descriptive, or contextual information.
Requests information needed to continue or decide.
Signals non-understanding, asks for repetition or clarification, or repairs a misunderstanding.
Confirms, checks, accepts, or rejects a detail or proposed outcome.
Responds to a constraint with an alternative, counter-proposal, compromise, or justified preference.
Creates, changes, cancels, or confirms an appointment, reservation, delivery, or other arrangement.
Obtains practical information, requirements, status, cost, location, schedule, or next steps.
Describes a problem with enough relevant information for the other party to act.
Requests and reaches a repair, replacement, refund, escalation, or other remedy.
Selects, orders, buys, exchanges, or returns a product or service while resolving required details.
Sustains appropriate small talk, invitation, apology, request, boundary, or social relationship work.
Gives a coherent account of self, experience, plans, or a familiar topic and handles follow-up.
Co-creates a plan by proposing, responding, agreeing, and confirming responsibilities and details.
Presents relevant experience, answers role questions, and obtains employment-process information.
Uses an understandable degree of politeness, directness, address, and channel convention.
Selects vocabulary sufficient and appropriate for the intended meaning.
Forms language accurately enough for the intended meaning at the claimed band.
Connects information so the exchange or presentation remains followable.
Notices and repairs or reformulates the learner's own contribution.
Produces useful language without copying a complete supplied answer.
